brief.headline: Close a ₹16.09 L/yr price gap to Mars Plastics and tighten payment terms to free up ₹10.63 L cash

priceAsk.summary: Match Mars Plastics' prices on the two big-volume items: ₹1.38/NOS for the 30 mL HDPE bottle and ₹0.81/NOS for the 28 mm PP cap
priceAsk.basis: We already pay Mars Plastics ₹1.38 for the 30 mL bottle (Premier charges ₹1.65, a 19.6% gap costing us ₹11.74 L/yr) and ₹0.81 for the cap (Premier charges ₹0.90, an 11.1% gap costing us ₹4.23 L/yr). The market asks ₹0.55–1.20 for a 28 mm induction-wad cap with a typical band of ₹0.85–0.95, and the verdict says there's modest headroom down to ₹0.65–0.80 at higher volume — so ₹0.81 is well inside fair territory.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Move from 45 days after receipt to 30 days
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: ₹10.63 L cash freed up for us

brief.financialLeverage: Premier Plastic publishes no financials, so we can't see their balance sheet or how tight cash is for them. Our ₹1.29 Cr annual spend is real business, but without knowing their total revenue we can't tell if we're 2% or 20% of their book. That means the plan leans on hard facts we do have: Mars Plastics' proven lower prices and the four strong alternates lined up below. Push firmly on price to close the ₹16.09 L gap, and on payment terms because 30 days is common in packaging. If they resist, name Manjushree or Mold-Tek as a second source we're qualifying — the threat of splitting volume will matter even if we can't quantify their dependence on us.

evidence.point: We pay Mars Plastics 19.6% less for the same 30 mL HDPE bottle
That one bottle SKU alone costs us an extra ₹11.74 L per year at Premier's price
We pay Mars Plastics 11.1% less for the 28 mm PP cap
The open-market asking band for a 28 mm induction-wad PP cap runs ₹0.55–1.20, with typical prices ₹0.85–0.95, and the verdict says modest headroom exists down to ₹0.65–0.80 at higher volume
Total extra cost across all rigid-plastic-packaging SKUs at Premier vs our best prices
Shortening payment terms from 45 days to 30 days frees up cash for us

alternates.name: Manjushree Technopack Ltd
alternates.why: India's largest rigid-plastic packaging converter (₹2569.83 Cr revenue), does pharma bottles, caps and preforms, health score B (65/100) — the top second-source candidate and already on our books for other packaging

alternates.name: Mold-Tek Packaging Ltd
alternates.why: Listed rigid-plastic leader (₹1010.97 Cr revenue) making pails, containers and pharma packaging, health B (73/100) — strong and profitable, a robust alternate for bottles and closures

alternates.name: Hitech Corporation Ltd
alternates.why: Listed, does moulded and blow-moulded packaging (₹701.17 Cr revenue), broad capability across bottles and caps, health C (51/100)

risks: Premier publishes no financials, so we're flying blind on their financial health and can't tell if a tough squeeze might push a fragile supplier over the edge — watch for any signs of distress in delivery performance and keep Manjushree warm as a safety valve

The ₹16.09 L gap is real but built on two SKUs (the 30 mL bottle and the 28 mm cap make up ₹15.97 L of it); if Premier walks on those line items we need Mars Plastics or an alternate ready to absorb the volume immediately

We have four qualified alternates and six market-backup leads (Reliance, IVL Dhunseri, Chemco, Srichakra, Dalmia, Ganesha Ecosphere), but every market lead must be verified and priced before we issue an RFQ — don't threaten to move volume to an unqualified source
Payment terms of 45 days aren't the worst we give anyone, so Premier may dig in; frame 30 days as the new normal and tie it to keeping their full volume rather than presenting it as a penalty
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We value the relationship, but Mars Plastics is giving us ₹1.38 on the 30 mL bottle and ₹0.81 on the cap — today we need to close that ₹16 lakh gap and move to 30-day terms so we can keep you as our lead source.
